blocks.source: Canto XXII
blocks.translation: Canto XXII

blocks.source: Io vidi già cavalier muover campo,
blocks.translation: I have erewhile seen horsemen moving camp,

blocks.source: e cominciare stormo e far lor mostra,
blocks.translation: Begin the battle, and their muster make,

blocks.source: e talvolta partir per loro scampo;
blocks.translation: And sometimes starting off for their escape;

blocks.source: corridor vidi per la terra vostra,
blocks.translation: Vaunt-couriers have I seen upon your land,

blocks.source: o Aretini, e vidi gir gualdane,
blocks.translation: O Aretines, and raiding parties go forth,

blocks.source: fedir torneamenti e correr giostra;
blocks.translation: Tournaments stricken, and the joustings run,

blocks.source: quando con trombe, e quando con campane,
blocks.translation: Sometimes with trumpets and sometimes with bells,

blocks.source: con tamburi e con cenni di castella,
blocks.translation: With kettle-drums, and signals of the castles,

blocks.source: e con cose nostrali e con istrane;
blocks.translation: And with our own, and with outlandish things,

blocks.source: né già con sì diversa cennamella
blocks.translation: But never yet with bagpipe so uncouth

blocks.source: cavalier vidi muover né pedoni,
blocks.translation: Did I see horsemen move, nor infantry,

blocks.source: né nave a segno di terra o di stella.
blocks.translation: Nor ship by any sign of land or star.

blocks.source: Noi andavam con li diece demoni.
blocks.translation: We went upon our way with the ten demons;

blocks.source: Ahi fiera compagnia! ma ne la chiesa
blocks.translation: Ah, savage company! but in the church

blocks.source: coi santi, e in taverna coi ghiottoni.
blocks.translation: With saints, and in the tavern with the gluttons!

blocks.source: Pur a la pegola era la mia ’ntesa,
blocks.translation: Ever upon the pitch was my intent,

blocks.source: per veder de la bolgia ogne contegno
blocks.translation: To see the whole condition of that Bolgia,

blocks.source: e de la gente ch’entro v’era incesa.
blocks.translation: And of the people who therein were burned.

blocks.source: Come i dalfini, quando fanno segno
blocks.translation: Even as the dolphins, when they make a sign

blocks.source: a’ marinar con l’arco de la schiena
blocks.translation: To mariners by arching of the back,

blocks.source: che s’argomentin di campar lor legno,
blocks.translation: That they should counsel take to save their vessel,

blocks.source: talor così, ad alleggiar la pena,
blocks.translation: Thus sometimes, to alleviate his pain,

blocks.source: mostrav’ alcun de’ peccatori ’l dosso
blocks.translation: One of the sinners would display his back,

blocks.source: e nascondea in men che non balena.
blocks.translation: And in less time conceal it than it lightens.

blocks.source: E come a l’orlo de l’acqua d’un fosso
blocks.translation: As on the brink of water in a ditch

blocks.source: stanno i ranocchi pur col muso fuori,
blocks.translation: The frogs stand only with their muzzles out,

blocks.source: sì che celano i piedi e l’altro grosso,
blocks.translation: So that they hide their feet and other bulk,

blocks.source: sì stavan d’ogne parte i peccatori;
blocks.translation: So upon every side the sinners stood;

blocks.source: ma come s’appressava Barbariccia,
blocks.translation: But ever as Barbariccia near them came,

blocks.source: così si ritraén sotto i bollori.
blocks.translation: Thus underneath the boiling they withdrew.

blocks.source: I’ vidi, e anco il cor me n’accapriccia,
blocks.translation: I saw, and still my heart doth shudder at it,

blocks.source: uno aspettar così, com’ elli ’ncontra
blocks.translation: One waiting thus, even as it comes to pass

blocks.source: ch’una rana rimane e l’altra spiccia;
blocks.translation: One frog remains, and down another dives;

blocks.source: e Graffiacan, che li era più di contra,
blocks.translation: And Graffiacan, who most confronted him,

blocks.source: li arruncigliò le ’mpegolate chiome
blocks.translation: Grappled him by his tresses smeared with pitch,

blocks.source: e trassel sù, che mi parve una lontra.
blocks.translation: And drew him up, so that he seemed an otter.

blocks.source: I’ sapea già di tutti quanti ’l nome,
blocks.translation: I knew, before, the names of all of them,

blocks.source: sì li notai quando fuorono eletti,
blocks.translation: So had I noted them when they were chosen,

blocks.source: e poi ch’e’ si chiamaro, attesi come.
blocks.translation: And when they called each other, listened how.

blocks.source: «O Rubicante, fa che tu li metti
blocks.translation: “O Rubicante, see that thou do lay

blocks.source: li unghioni a dosso, sì che tu lo scuoi!»,
blocks.translation: Thy claws upon him, so that thou mayst flay him,”

blocks.source: gridavan tutti insieme i maladetti.
blocks.translation: Cried all together the accursed ones.

blocks.source: E io: «Maestro mio, fa, se tu puoi,
blocks.translation: And I: “My Master, see to it, if thou canst,

blocks.source: che tu sappi chi è lo sciagurato
blocks.translation: That thou mayst know who is the luckless wight,

blocks.source: venuto a man de li avversari suoi».
blocks.translation: Thus come into his adversaries’ hands.”

blocks.source: Lo duca mio li s’accostò allato;
blocks.translation: Near to the side of him my Leader drew,

blocks.source: domandollo ond’ ei fosse, e quei rispuose:
blocks.translation: Asked of him whence he was; and he replied:

blocks.source: «I’ fui del regno di Navarra nato.
blocks.translation: “I in the kingdom of Navarre was born;

blocks.source: Mia madre a servo d’un segnor mi puose,
blocks.translation: My mother placed me servant to a lord,

blocks.source: che m’avea generato d’un ribaldo,
blocks.translation: For she had borne me to a ribald knave,

blocks.source: distruggitor di sé e di sue cose.
blocks.translation: Destroyer of himself and of his things.

blocks.source: Poi fui famiglia del buon re Tebaldo;
blocks.translation: Then I domestic was of good King Thibault;

blocks.source: quivi mi misi a far baratteria,
blocks.translation: I set me there to practise barratry,

blocks.source: di ch’io rendo ragione in questo caldo».
blocks.translation: For which I pay the reckoning in this heat.”

blocks.source: E Cirïatto, a cui di bocca uscia
blocks.translation: And Ciriatto, from whose mouth projected,

blocks.source: d’ogne parte una sanna come a porco,
blocks.translation: On either side, a tusk, as in a boar,

blocks.source: li fé sentir come l’una sdruscia.
blocks.translation: Caused him to feel how one of them could rip.

blocks.source: Tra male gatte era venuto ’l sorco;
blocks.translation: Among malicious cats the mouse had come;

blocks.source: ma Barbariccia il chiuse con le braccia
blocks.translation: But Barbariccia clasped him in his arms,

blocks.source: e disse: «State in là, mentr’ io lo ’nforco».
blocks.translation: And said: “Stand ye aside, while I enfork him.”

blocks.source: E al maestro mio volse la faccia;
blocks.translation: And to my Master he turned round his head;

blocks.source: «Domanda», disse, «ancor, se più disii
blocks.translation: “Ask him again,” he said, “if more thou wish

blocks.source: saper da lui, prima ch’altri ’l disfaccia».
blocks.translation: To know from him, before some one destroy him.”

blocks.source: Lo duca dunque: «Or dì: de li altri rii
blocks.translation: The Guide: “Now tell then of the other culprits;

blocks.source: conosci tu alcun che sia latino
blocks.translation: Knowest thou any one who is a Latian,

blocks.source: sotto la pece?». E quelli: «I’ mi partii,
blocks.translation: Under the pitch?”  And he: “I separated

blocks.source: poco è, da un che fu di là vicino.
blocks.translation: Lately from one who was a neighbour to it;

blocks.source: Così foss’ io ancor con lui coperto,
blocks.translation: Would that I still were covered up with him,

blocks.source: ch’i’ non temerei unghia né uncino!».
blocks.translation: For I should fear not either claw nor hook!”

blocks.source: E Libicocco «Troppo avem sofferto»,
blocks.translation: And Libicocco: “We have borne too much;”

blocks.source: disse; e preseli ’l braccio col runciglio,
blocks.translation: And with his grapnel seized him by the arm,

blocks.source: sì che, stracciando, ne portò un lacerto.
blocks.translation: So that, by rending, he tore off a piece of flesh.

blocks.source: Draghignazzo anco i volle dar di piglio
blocks.translation: Eke Draghignazzo wished to pounce upon him

blocks.source: giuso a le gambe; onde ’l decurio loro
blocks.translation: Down at the legs; whence their Decurion

blocks.source: si volse intorno intorno con mal piglio.
blocks.translation: Turned round and round about with evil look.

blocks.source: Quand’ elli un poco rappaciati fuoro,
blocks.translation: When they again somewhat were pacified,

blocks.source: a lui, ch’ancor mirava sua ferita,
blocks.translation: Of him, who still was looking at his wound,

blocks.source: domandò ’l duca mio sanza dimoro:
blocks.translation: Demanded my Conductor without stay:

blocks.source: «Chi fu colui da cui mala partita
blocks.translation: “Who was that one, from whom a luckless parting

blocks.source: di’ che facesti per venire a proda?».
blocks.translation: Thou sayest thou hast made, to come ashore?”

blocks.source: Ed ei rispuose: «Fu frate Gomita,
blocks.translation: And he replied: “It was the Friar Gomita,

blocks.source: quel di Gallura, vasel d’ogne froda,
blocks.translation: He of Gallura, vessel of all fraud,

blocks.source: ch’ebbe i nemici di suo donno in mano,
blocks.translation: Who had the enemies of his Lord in hand,

blocks.source: e fé sì lor, che ciascun se ne loda.
blocks.translation: And dealt so with them each exults thereat;

blocks.source: Danar si tolse e lasciolli di piano,
blocks.translation: Money he took, and let them smoothly off,

blocks.source: sì com’ e’ dice; e ne li altri offici anche
blocks.translation: As he says; and in other offices

blocks.source: barattier fu non picciol, ma sovrano.
blocks.translation: A barrator was he, not mean but sovereign.

blocks.source: Usa con esso donno Michel Zanche
blocks.translation: Foregathers with him one Don Michael Zanche

blocks.source: di Logodoro; e a dir di Sardigna
blocks.translation: Of Logodoro; and of Sardinia

blocks.source: le lingue lor non si sentono stanche.
blocks.translation: To gossip never do their tongues feel tired.

blocks.source: Omè, vedete l’altro che digrigna;
blocks.translation: O me! see that one, how he grinds his teeth;

blocks.source: i’ direi anche, ma i’ temo ch’ello
blocks.translation: Still farther would I speak, but am afraid

blocks.source: non s’apparecchi a grattarmi la tigna».
blocks.translation: Lest he to scratch my itch be making ready.”

blocks.source: E ’l gran proposto, vòlto a Farfarello
blocks.translation: And the grand Provost, turned to Farfarello,

blocks.source: che stralunava li occhi per fedire,
blocks.translation: Who rolled his eyes about as if to strike,

blocks.source: disse: «Fatti ’n costà, malvagio uccello!».
blocks.translation: Said: “Stand aside there, thou malicious bird.”

blocks.source: «Se voi volete vedere o udire»,
blocks.translation: “If you desire either to see or hear,”

blocks.source: ricominciò lo spaürato appresso,
blocks.translation: The terror-stricken recommenced thereon,

blocks.source: «Toschi o Lombardi, io ne farò venire;
blocks.translation: “Tuscans or Lombards, I will make them come.

blocks.source: ma stieno i Malebranche un poco in cesso,
blocks.translation: But let the Malebranche cease a little,

blocks.source: sì ch’ei non teman de le lor vendette;
blocks.translation: So that these may not their revenges fear,

blocks.source: e io, seggendo in questo loco stesso,
blocks.translation: And I, down sitting in this very place,

blocks.source: per un ch’io son, ne farò venir sette
blocks.translation: For one that I am will make seven come,

blocks.source: quand’ io suffolerò, com’ è nostro uso
blocks.translation: When I shall whistle, as our custom is

blocks.source: di fare allor che fori alcun si mette».
blocks.translation: To do whenever one of us comes out.”

blocks.source: Cagnazzo a cotal motto levò ’l muso,
blocks.translation: Cagnazzo at these words his muzzle lifted,

blocks.source: crollando ’l capo, e disse: «Odi malizia
blocks.translation: Shaking his head, and said: “Just hear the trick

blocks.source: ch’elli ha pensata per gittarsi giuso!».
blocks.translation: Which he has thought of, down to throw himself!”

blocks.source: Ond’ ei, ch’avea lacciuoli a gran divizia,
blocks.translation: Whence he, who snares in great abundance had,

blocks.source: rispuose: «Malizioso son io troppo,
blocks.translation: Responded: “I by far too cunning am,

blocks.source: quand’ io procuro a’ mia maggior trestizia».
blocks.translation: When I procure for mine a greater sadness.”

blocks.source: Alichin non si tenne e, di rintoppo
blocks.translation: Alichin held not in, but running counter

blocks.source: a li altri, disse a lui: «Se tu ti cali,
blocks.translation: Unto the rest, said to him: “If thou dive,

blocks.source: io non ti verrò dietro di gualoppo,
blocks.translation: I will not follow thee upon the gallop,

blocks.source: ma batterò sovra la pece l’ali.
blocks.translation: But I will beat my wings above the pitch;

blocks.source: Lascisi ’l collo, e sia la ripa scudo,
blocks.translation: The height be left, and be the bank a shield

blocks.source: a veder se tu sol più di noi vali».
blocks.translation: To see if thou alone dost countervail us.”

blocks.source: O tu che leggi, udirai nuovo ludo:
blocks.translation: O thou who readest, thou shalt hear new sport!

blocks.source: ciascun da l’altra costa li occhi volse,
blocks.translation: Each to the other side his eyes averted;

blocks.source: quel prima, ch’a ciò fare era più crudo.
blocks.translation: He first, who most reluctant was to do it.

blocks.source: Lo Navarrese ben suo tempo colse;
blocks.translation: The Navarrese selected well his time;

blocks.source: fermò le piante a terra, e in un punto
blocks.translation: Planted his feet on land, and in a moment

blocks.source: saltò e dal proposto lor si sciolse.
blocks.translation: Leaped, and escaped from their commander’s grasp.

blocks.source: Di che ciascun di colpa fu compunto,
blocks.translation: Whereat each one was suddenly stung with shame,

blocks.source: ma quei più che cagion fu del difetto;
blocks.translation: But he most who was cause of the defeat;

blocks.source: però si mosse e gridò: «Tu se’ giunto!».
blocks.translation: Therefore he moved, and cried: “Thou art o’ertakern.”

blocks.source: Ma poco i valse: ché l’ali al sospetto
blocks.translation: But little it availed, for wings could not

blocks.source: non potero avanzar; quelli andò sotto,
blocks.translation: Outstrip the fear; the other one went under,

blocks.source: e quei drizzò volando suso il petto:
blocks.translation: And, flying, upward he his breast directed;

blocks.source: non altrimenti l’anitra di botto,
blocks.translation: Not otherwise the duck upon a sudden

blocks.source: quando ’l falcon s’appressa, giù s’attuffa,
blocks.translation: Dives under, when the falcon is approaching,

blocks.source: ed ei ritorna sù crucciato e rotto.
blocks.translation: And upward he returneth cross and weary.

blocks.source: Irato Calcabrina de la buffa,
blocks.translation: Infuriate at the mockery, Calcabrina

blocks.source: volando dietro li tenne, invaghito
blocks.translation: Flying behind him followed close, desirous

blocks.source: che quei campasse per aver la zuffa;
blocks.translation: The other should escape, to have a quarrel.

blocks.source: e come ’l barattier fu disparito,
blocks.translation: And when the barrator had disappeared,

blocks.source: così volse li artigli al suo compagno,
blocks.translation: He turned his talons upon his companion,

blocks.source: e fu con lui sopra ’l fosso ghermito.
blocks.translation: And grappled with him right above the moat.

blocks.source: Ma l’altro fu bene sparvier grifagno
blocks.translation: But sooth the other was a doughty sparhawk

blocks.source: ad artigliar ben lui, e amendue
blocks.translation: To clapperclaw him well; and both of them

blocks.source: cadder nel mezzo del bogliente stagno.
blocks.translation: Fell in the middle of the boiling pond.

blocks.source: Lo caldo sghermitor sùbito fue;
blocks.translation: A sudden intercessor was the heat;

blocks.source: ma però di levarsi era neente,
blocks.translation: But ne’ertheless of rising there was naught,

blocks.source: sì avieno inviscate l’ali sue.
blocks.translation: To such degree they had their wings belimed.

blocks.source: Barbariccia, con li altri suoi dolente,
blocks.translation: Lamenting with the others, Barbariccia

blocks.source: quattro ne fé volar da l’altra costa
blocks.translation: Made four of them fly to the other side

blocks.source: con tutt’ i raffi, e assai prestamente
blocks.translation: With all their gaffs, and very speedily

blocks.source: di qua, di là discesero a la posta;
blocks.translation: This side and that they to their posts descended;

blocks.source: porser li uncini verso li ’mpaniati,
blocks.translation: They stretched their hooks towards the pitch-ensnared,

blocks.source: ch’eran già cotti dentro da la crosta.
blocks.translation: Who were already baked within the crust,

blocks.source: E noi lasciammo lor così ’mpacciati.
blocks.translation: And in this manner busied did we leave them.
